## DATA description 
o\*net is dataset about the occupations and their characteristics in the U.S. Based on my project about the relationship between occupations and skills required by occupations, I chose this dataset including the major types of occupations (occupation group, preparation level), occupation codes and titles, 35 occupation skills, education level required by the occupations, and the skill dimension I extarcted before. Specifically, for each skill, we have a score for their importance in this occupation from 0-5 (continuous variables), and other variables are categorical variables. I chose 3 skills in each factor dimension, so we have 12 skills in total. 
Specifically, we have:
  1. occupation unique codes and titles 
  2. job zone (the preparation level needed before people enter these occupations)
  3. occupation groups (the major type of occupations)
  4. scores on skill dimensions
  5. scores on 12 specific skills
  
## Read data
```{r}
#read data
library(tidyverse)
data <- read.csv("onet_2026_clean.csv") |>
  mutate (preparation = factor(job_zone, levels = c("Little","Medium","Considerable","Extensive" )))

```


## Contingency tables - categorical variables
```{r}
# investigate data
table(data$job_zone)
table(data$major_group)
table(data$skill_type)

table(data$preparation, data$major_group)
table(data$major_group, data$skill_type)
table(data$preparation, data$skill_type)

```
```{r}
# investigate data - summarize the continous variables
# write a function to make good programming 
summarise_onet <- function(x){
  data |> 
    group_by(.data[[x]]) |>
    summarise(across(where(is.numeric), list(mean = mean, median = median, sd = sd)))
}
summarise_onet("preparation")
summarise_onet("skill_type")
summarise_onet("major_group")
```

## Bar Chart
```{r}
# bar chart 
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data, 
       aes(x = skill_type)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Occupations distributions by skill dimension",
       x = "Skill dimension", y = "Number of occupations")

```
Occupations who focus on technical skills have the most amounts, while who focus on the analytival skills have the least. 

## Side by side bar chart plot 
```{r}

ggplot(data,
       aes(x = skill_type, fill = major_group)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Occuparion occupation group by skill dimension",
       x = "skill dimensions", y = "Number of Occuaptions",
       fill = "Occupation occupation group")

```
For the analytically-based occuparions, they are concentrated on STEM occupation group; for the communication-based occupations, they are concentrated in Education, legal, soial& arts, and Healthcare occupation groups; for the management-based occupations, they are concentrated in many occupation groups, especially business; for the technical-based occupation group, they are concentrated in construction, production and transport, so the technical skills are actually mechnical skills from this point. 


## Histogram Plot - numerical variables
```{r}

ggplot(data,
       aes(x = analytical)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(title = "Analytical scores",
       x = "Analytical-skil scores",
       y = "Number of occupartions")

```
The distribution of the analytical skill scores is right-skewed. The peak of analytically skill scores is lower than 0 (the average), too. More than half of the occupations' analytical scores are lower than the average. 

## Histogram plot (facted version)

```{r}



ggplot(data,
       aes(x = analytical, fill = preparation)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_wrap(~preparation) +
  labs(title = "Analytical scores by preparation level of occupations",
       x = "Analytical-skil scores",
       y = "Number of occupartions",
       fill = "Preparation levels")

```
Analytical scores are increasing as the preparation level improves.

## Box plot
```{r}

ggplot(data,
       aes(x = analytical, y = major_group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Box Plot of analytical scores by occupation group",
       y = "occupation group",
       x = "Analytical scores")

```


## Heatmap

```{r}
data |>
  group_by(major_group) |>
 summarise(across(c(communication, technical, analytical, management), mean)) |>
  pivot_longer(-major_group, names_to = "skills", values_to = "mean") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = skills, y = major_group, fill = mean)) +
  geom_tile(color = "blue") +
  scale_fill_gradient() +
  labs(title = "Average skill scores on each dimension by occupation group",
       x = "skill dimension", y = "occupation group", fill = "Mean score")
```
Each occupation group relies most on one skill dimension: STEM on analytical skill, management and business on management skill; healthcare and education on communication skill; construction, production, and transport on technical skill.
